rule: The Dominican Republic has two modes: Regla General (like the Latin game, no bonuses listed) and Regla de Patio (informal). Patio mode carries the pase de salida, pase corrido, and capicúa bonuses.
quote: se juegan dos modalidades, son llamadas De Regla General y De Regla de Patio
sourceName: Wikipedia (es), Dominó dominicano

rule: Patio play uses one table even with three or more pairs; the losing pair gives up its seat, so the rules aim to speed play.
quote: se usa solo una mesa aunque haya tres o más parejas
sourceName: Wikipedia (es), Dominó dominicano

rule: 'Juego en banda': a position where the tranque is forced no matter where the remaining tiles are played.
quote: el tranque es obligado sin importar por donde se coloquen las fichas restantes
sourceName: Wikipedia (es), Dominó dominicano

rule: Pintintín: a Dominican every-player-for-himself variant for 2 to 4 players with 6 or 7 tiles each. It is played for bets, with no running score.
quote: El Pintintin es una variedad en la que se juega todos contra todos.
sourceName: Wikipedia (es), Dominó dominicano

rule: A player of the losing team shuffles the tiles for the next hand (the 'dar agua' custom).
quote: Un jugador del equipo perdedor le tocara barajar las fichas.
sourceName: Wikipedia (es), Dominó dominicano

rule: Tile names: in the Dominican Republic the double blank is 'la caja' and the double six is 'el burro'.
quote: en República Dominicana el cero doble se conoce como «la caja»
sourceName: Wikipedia (es), Dominó, Nombre de las fichas

rule: A Dominican columnist names the double blank 'la cajita' or 'el muerto', not 'la chucha'.
quote: El doble blanco es la cajita o el muerto
sourceName: Diario Libre, Aníbal de Castro (2026)

rule: Dominican players keep rules that differ by local custom.
quote: En el español dominicano los jugadores mantienen reglas que difieren según las costumbres.
sourceName: Acento, Roberto Guzmán (2025)

rule: The Dominican verb for shuffling tiles is 'barajar las fichas'.
quote: “barajar las fichas” es mezclarlas antes de repartirlas
sourceName: Acento, Roberto Guzmán (2025)

rule: FichaFlow says chuchazo comes from Puerto Rican rules and pollona is a Cuban shutout term; both are off by default. Its pollona page reports no reliable standard Dominican pollona bonus.
quote: Chuchazo is documented in Puerto Rican rules and Pollona as a Cuban shutout term
sourceName: FichaFlow

rule: Puerto Rico: la Chucha is the 0-0. A chuchazo (going out with it) earns a 100-point prize only in 500-point games.
quote: 100 puntos de premio solo en mesas de 500 puntos
sourceName: Mesa28, Qué es un chuchazo en dominó boricua

rule: Santiago tournament: sudden death, so the losing pair leaves (patio style). Rule 7 says a hand with five doubles is still played.
quote: SE JUGARA MUERTE SUBITA, EL QUE PERDIO SE VA.
sourceName: Momento Deportivo RD, Copa Alcaldía de Santiago rules (2019)

rule: La Guáyiga tournament: tiles are reshuffled only if the 7 doubles come out (together in one hand). Other deals are played as dealt.
quote: Solo se baraja si salen los 7 dobles.
sourceName: Junta del Distrito Municipal La Guáyiga (2025)

rule: Three-player Dominican game: 7 tiles each with 7 out of play, every man for himself, first to 200.
quote: three people with 7 cards each, and 7 out of play
sourceName: DR1.com forum (2013)

rule: One tournament-listing site claims the FEDOMDOM cup uses double-9 with a 'pollona' penalty. Every other Dominican source describes double six, so this claim is likely wrong.
quote: Las reglas siguen la variante dominicana, que usa el doble-9
sourceName: jugardominoenlinea.com, Torneos de Dominó

rule: The Dominican Republic has two modes: Regla General (formal) and Regla de Patio (informal).
quote: se juegan dos modalidades, son llamadas De Regla General y De Regla de Patio
sourceName: Wikipedia (es), Dominó, section Dominó dominicano

rule: Regla general is essentially the generic Latino mode. The bonuses (capicúa, pase corrido, puntos de salida) are listed under the patio mode.
quote: El dominó de regla general es más bien la modalidad latina.
sourceName: Wikipedia (es), Dominó, section Dominó dominicano

rule: Juego de patio: one table is shared by three or more pairs. The winners stay and the losers give their place to the next pair, so there are rules and penalties to speed up play.
quote: para seguir jugando hay que ganar las partidas o si no, ceder el turno
sourceName: Wikipedia (es), Dominó, section Dominó dominicano

rule: A player from the losing team shuffles the tiles for the next hand.
quote: Un jugador del equipo perdedor le tocara barajar las fichas.
sourceName: Wikipedia (es), Dominó, section Dominó dominicano

rule: Pintintín: an every-player-for-himself Dominican variant for 2 to 4 players with 6 or 7 tiles each. It is a betting game and each hand stands alone, with no cumulative score.
quote: El Pintintin es una variedad en la que se juega todos contra todos.
sourceName: Wikipedia (es), Dominó, section Dominó dominicano

rule: Dominican names for tiles: the double blank is 'la caja' and the double six is 'el burro'.
quote: en República Dominicana el cero doble se conoce como «la caja»
sourceName: Wikipedia (es), Dominó, section Nombres de las fichas

rule: Santiago 2019 municipal tournament rules claim to apply 'international rules', yet add a 25-point capicúa and a 25-point pase de salida and give no points for the pase corrido. This mixes federation rules with local bonuses.
quote: aplicándose las reglas internacional que rige este deporte
sourceName: Momento Deportivo RD, Copa Alcaldía de Santiago (2019)

rule: Santiago 2019: a hand is played even with five doubles, so there is no reshuffle for doubles.
quote: CINCO BOBLE SE JUEGA.
sourceName: Momento Deportivo RD, Copa Alcaldía de Santiago rules (2019)

rule: Santiago 2019: passing with a playable tile, or a 'chivo'/'pacho' (a tile that does not fit), is a 100-point swing: -50 to the offenders and +50 to the other pair. Then the tiles are reshuffled and the next opener in rotation opens.
quote: PASO CON FICHA SON 100 PUNTOS
sourceName: Momento Deportivo RD, Copa Alcaldía de Santiago rules (2019)

rule: La Guáyiga 2025: the tiles are reshuffled only if 'the 7 doubles come out'. In practice a hand with many doubles must be played.
quote: Solo se baraja si salen los 7 dobles.
sourceName: Junta del Distrito Municipal La Guáyiga, tournament rules (2025)

rule: FEMUNDO: the hand is played with all the doubles a player draws, so there is no reshuffle for many doubles.
quote: Se jugará con todos los dobles que el atleta levante.
sourceName: FEMUNDO, Reglamento de Competencia 2025 (Art. 5)

rule: US tournament association: a player who draws 5 or more doubles may show them and have the tiles reshuffled, and the same player opens again.
quote: SI UN JUGADOR COJE 5 O MAS DOBLES TIENE LA OPCION DE VIRARLAS
sourceName: NEUSA Domino Association, Reglamento de los torneos (rev. 2010)

rule: Dominican custom: when the opener (mano) makes the opponent on his right pass, the opener's partner becomes the 'manito'. Spectators may not comment ('los mirones son de cera').
quote: su frente se convierte en “manito”
sourceName: Acento.com.do, Roberto Guzmán, 'Dominó' (2025)

rule: Chuchazo (going out with the double blank) is a Puerto Rican bonus worth +100 in the 500-point game. It does not apply when the double blank is the tile that locks a tranque.
quote: There is no "Chuchazo" when the "Tranque" in a blocked game is the "Chucha".
sourceName: José Carrillo, 'Domino Games in Puerto Rico' (archived)

rule: Puerto Rico: the shutout term is 'chiva' or 'chivote' (for example 200-0), not 'pollona'.
quote: A term for "kept winless" or "shutout"
sourceName: José Carrillo, 'Domino Games in Puerto Rico' (archived)

rule: The Diccionario de americanismos labels 'pollona' only as Cuban: losing a domino game without scoring any points.
quote: pérdida de una partida sin lograr acumular ningún punto
sourceName: ASALE, Diccionario de americanismos, 'pollona'

rule: App: chuchazo is documented in Puerto Rican rules and pollona as a Cuban shutout term. Both are optional and off by default for Dominican play.
quote: Chuchazo is documented in Puerto Rican rules, and Pollona as a Cuban shutout term
sourceName: FichaFlow, 'Complete Dominican Domino Guide'

rule: Federation context: in 2010, Puerto Rico and the Dominican Republic split from the FID and organized their own parallel world championships (the FEMUNDO line).
quote: organizando sus porpios mundiales paralelos
sourceName: Jugamos Todos, 'Mundiales de Dominó'

rule: The Federación Dominicana de Dominó (Fededodo) ran its 2025 National Championship over 14 official matches to select the team for the FEMUNDO 2025 world championship. This implies that its national tournaments use the FEMUNDO/FID-style rules, with no bonuses. No published Fededodo rulebook was found.
quote: 14 partidas oficiales
sourceName: Diario Libre, 'Mundial de dóminos en Barbados tendrá participación RD' (2025)

rule: The Dominican Republic has two modalities: Regla General (close to Latin dominó) and Regla de Patio (informal). The patio bonuses (salida, corrido, capicúa) belong to the informal mode.
quote: se juegan dos modalidades, son llamadas De Regla General y De Regla de Patio
sourceName: Wikipedia (es), Dominó dominicano

rule: La Mesa: in more formal rules (Regla General) capicúa earns nothing; it is a patio-game bonus.
quote: En las reglas más formales, tipo Regla General, la capicúa no se premia
sourceName: La Mesa: Dominó Latino, ¿Qué es la capicúa?

rule: Patio game: one table serves several pairs; a pair must keep winning or give up its seat to the next pair.
quote: para seguir jugando hay que ganar las partidas o si no, ceder el turno
sourceName: Wikipedia (es), Dominó dominicano, Juego de patio

rule: 'Juego en banda': a hand where the tranque is forced because the remaining player(s) must give the tiles that lock it.
quote: es aquel en el que el tranque es obligado
sourceName: Wikipedia (es), Dominó dominicano, Juego en banda

rule: Tile names: in the Dominican Republic the double blank is called 'la caja' and the double six 'el burro'.
quote: en República Dominicana el cero doble se conoce como «la caja»
sourceName: Wikipedia (es), Dominó, Nombre de las fichas

rule: La Mesa: the Dominican word for shuffling face down before dealing is 'lavar' (not 'dar agua').
quote: se revuelven las fichas boca abajo (eso es lavar el dominó)
sourceName: La Mesa: Dominó Latino, Reglas del dominó dominicano

rule: FichaFlow: chuchazo (going out with 0-0) is documented in Puerto Rican Quinientos at +100. FichaFlow found no basis for it as a standard Dominican bonus, keeps it off by default, and never stacks it with capicúa.
quote: We found no basis to call it a standard Dominican bonus.
sourceName: FichaFlow, What Is Chuchazo?

rule: FichaFlow classifies chuchazo as Puerto Rican and pollona as a Cuban shutout term; both optional bonuses start at 0.
quote: Chuchazo is documented in Puerto Rican rules and Pollona as a Cuban shutout term
sourceName: FichaFlow, How to Play Dominican Domino

rule: La Mesa's Dominican glossary defines chuchazo as a hard hit on the rivals (for example going out fast and leaving them loaded), not as a specific tile.
quote: Un golpe fuerte en la mesa
sourceName: La Mesa: Dominó Latino, Glosario del dominó dominicano

rule: La Mesa glossary: zapato (zapatero) means winning the whole game while the other pair scores zero; some tables also call it pollona.
quote: También se le dice pollona en algunas mesas.
sourceName: La Mesa: Dominó Latino, Glosario del dominó dominicano

rule: Diccionario de americanismos: pollona is losing a domino match without scoring any points, marked as Cuban usage only.
quote: pérdida de una partida sin lograr acumular ningún punto
sourceName: ASALE, Diccionario de americanismos, 'pollona'

rule: Domino Apunte Dominicano celebrates a 200-0 win with 'LISA y ZAPATERA' (shutout names in Dominican play).
quote: gana 200-0, la pantalla explota con la legendaria celebración de LISA y ZAPATERA
sourceName: Domino Apunte Dominicano (Google Play listing)

rule: Mesa28 (Puerto Rico): la Chucha is the 0-0; a chuchazo is going out with it, unless it closes two blank ends (then it is dominau). Worth 100 only in 500 games.
quote: La Chucha es la ficha 0-0.
sourceName: Mesa28, Qué es un chuchazo en dominó boricua

rule: La Guáyiga tournament penalties: 30 to the other team for playing a tile that does not match ('un chivo'), for playing out of turn, and for opening out of turn. A lifted tile must be played.
quote: Si tiras una ficha que no cuadra (“un chivo”): +30 pts al equipo contrario.
sourceName: Junta del Distrito Municipal La Guáyiga, Gran Torneo de Dominó Regular 3/2

rule: La Guáyiga tournament: the tiles are reshuffled only if the 7 doubles come out (the flyer does not explain this further).
quote: Solo se baraja si salen los 7 dobles.
sourceName: Junta del Distrito Municipal La Guáyiga, Gran Torneo de Dominó Regular 3/2

rule: Santiago tournament (2019): a hand with five doubles is still played; a wrong opening gives 50 to the opponents; asking about the opening is allowed.
quote: CINCO BOBLE SE JUEGA.
sourceName: Momento Deportivo RD, Reglas del torneo Copa Alcaldía de Santiago 2019

rule: Dominican table custom: onlookers must not comment on the play.
quote: “los mirones son de cera”
sourceName: Acento, 'Dominó' (language column)

rule: Dominator scorekeeper names the two Dominican teams 'Largos' and 'Cortos' by default.
quote: Two side-by-side team columns (Largos & Cortos) that mirror the table.
sourceName: Dominator - apunte de domino (Google Play listing)

rule: FichaFlow uses 'Veinticinco' as the settings name for the pase de salida bonus, and says the name does not force a 25-point value.

sourceName: FichaFlow, What Is Pase de Salida in Domino?

rule: Santiago tournament (2019): sudden death, the losing pair leaves the table (patio style).

sourceName: Momento Deportivo RD, 1er Torneo de Dominó Copa Alcaldía de Santiago reglamento (2019)

rule: La Guáyiga tournament (2025): reshuffle only if all 7 doubles come out (in one hand); penalties of +30 to the other team for a tile that does not fit (chivo), playing out of turn, etc.

sourceName: Junta del Distrito Municipal La Guáyiga, Gran Torneo de Dominó Regular 3/2 (2025)

rule: La Guáyiga tournament (2025): playing a tile that does not fit (a chivo) gives 30 points to the other team.

sourceName: Junta del Distrito Municipal La Guáyiga, Gran Torneo de Dominó Regular 3/2 (2025)

rule: Forum (2006): Dominicans add extra points for certain situations such as capicúa and 'caja de muerto' (not defined in the post).

sourceName: DR1.com forum, Rules for playing domino, user Mirador, 2006

rule: Forum (2013): in some places you lose points for making noise or if a tile falls on the floor.
quote: you also lose points in one of your cards falls on the floor
sourceName: DR1.com forum, Rules for Dominican Dominoes?, user The Gorgon, 2013

rule: FID international regulation: a hand ends only by dominada or by cierre/tranca; the regulation contains no capicúa or pass bonuses (only tile points and penalties).
quote: Toda mano o ronda termina por dominada, por cierre o tranca.
sourceName: Federación Internacional de Dominó, Reglamento (2024), Art. 54
